entries.rationale: `conclear release` runs the complete fail-closed workflow from a reviewed revision to verified promotion.
Every run builds from a detached worktree of the selected committed revision and takes trust configuration from the release profile.
There is no CI mode; the same commands produce a complete release on a maintainer workstation.
Source runs check out the selected commit into a run-owned detached worktree, so uncommitted and untracked files never enter the build.
`conclear check` runs the source, configuration, Containerfile and context checks before any build.
`conclear pins check` validates declared image inputs and pins before qualification.
`conclear qualify` builds, imports, re-verifies and tests `linux/amd64` first and records the execution mode; configuration without that platform is rejected.
Qualification repeats the same sequence for every other declared platform, locally or on a worker.
`conclear assemble` aggregates accepted qualifications into the release candidate and `conclear provenance` derives the predicate from that record.
Buildah is invoked with `--format oci` for every build.
Runtime tests run through rootless Podman.
Repository configuration must list `linux/amd64`; qualification and publication cover every listed platform.
Hadolint (`CC0114`) reports syntax it knows to be unsupported; conformance to the Containerfile manual otherwise needs review.
Native execution per platform is a repository decision (`native_test_platforms`); whether an image needs it is judgment.
Tool versions on workstations and CI runners are managed by the organization; ConClear records what it resolved.
Pinning supporting tools is a repository decision; ConClear records resolved versions and tool-image digests.
`linux/arm64` is qualified natively or under QEMU when configured.
Builds, tests and releases use Buildah, Podman and Skopeo only; no Docker daemon or BuildKit is involved (GO0003).
A Docker compatibility claim is project documentation outside ConClear's scope.
`conclear version` prints the tool version, source revision and the implemented guide identity.
Both identities are embedded at build time and never read from the repository under test.
Every record carries the `ruleset` object defined by the record schemas.
The check catalog maps every check to requirement identifiers and the generated conformance document states a status for every identifier.
The generated conformance document lists the built-in limits.
Manual checks (`CC9nnn`) are listed as manual; no mechanical check claims them.
